title: SWEAR: Section-Wise Efficient Audio Reasoning via Self-Rated Difficulty
abstract: arXiv:2610.13081v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Recent work on large audio-language models (LALMs) explores adaptive reasoning to balance accuracy and efficiency. However, existing approaches often rely on coarse-grained difficulty estimation, overlooking the diverse factors that determine reasoning effort. We address this limitation by deriving five-dimensional difficulty scores and compressed reasoning traces from complementary offline assessments. Based on this characterization, we propose SWEAR, a difficulty-aware reasoning framework that learns difficulty signals during supervised fine-tuning and uses reinforcement learning to adapt reasoning allocation across reasoning stages. Experiments on MMAU-test-mini and MMAR show that SWEAR improves accuracy while substantially reducing generated tokens, shortening reasoning for easy instances without sacrificing performance on difficult ones.

translated_title: SWEAR：基于自评难度的分段式高效音频推理
translated_abstract: 近期关于大型音频-语言模型（LALMs）的研究探索了自适应推理，以在准确性与效率之间取得平衡。然而，现有方法通常依赖粗粒度的难度估计，忽视了决定推理工作量的多样化因素。为解决这一局限，我们从互补的离线评估中推导出五维难度分数和压缩的推理轨迹。基于这种刻画方式，我们提出了SWEAR——一个难度感知的推理框架，它在监督微调阶段学习难度信号，并利用强化学习在各个推理阶段之间自适应地分配推理资源。在MMAU-test-mini和MMAR数据集上的实验表明，SWEAR在大幅减少生成token数量的同时提高了准确率，在不牺牲困难样本性能的前提下缩短了简单样本的推理过程。
tldr: SWEAR提出了一种难度感知的音频推理框架，通过五维难度评分和强化学习在推理各阶段自适应分配推理资源，在大幅减少生成token的同时提升准确率，简单样本推理更快而不损失困难样本的性能。
en_tdlr: SWEAR is a difficulty-aware audio reasoning framework that learns five-dimensional difficulty signals via supervised fine-tuning and uses reinforcement learning to adaptively allocate reasoning effort across stages, improving accuracy while substantially reducing generated tokens.
